hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes training into divergence (e.g. #68 lost 13 to 27 points).
Lowering an unstable high learning rate restores stable training (e.g. #74 and #80 gained 9 to 48 points).
Very small learning rates leave the network undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps (#61 and #63).
Decreasing an already tiny learning rate worsens undertraining.
Very strong L2 (alpha near 1) underfits, so weakening it helps (#10 gained 2 to 8 points).
Increasing already heavy regularization worsens underfitting (#16 lost about 5 points on two datasets).
With tiny learning rates, extra layers add capacity and speed up progress rather than causing instability (#51, #55, #59).
Wider layers learn faster at small learning rates, which helps when training is otherwise slow (#86, #91).
Smaller batches make noisier gradients, which tips high-learning-rate runs into divergence (#32, #36).
Deeper networks are more fragile at large learning rates, so removing a layer stabilizes training (#53).
